newsitem.title: USA: Hormone therapy may cut cholesterol in women - study.
newsitem.headline: Hormone therapy may cut cholesterol in women - study.

text.p: Women past the age of menopause can be treated for high cholesterol with hormone replacement therapy, according to a study published in the American Medical Association's Archives of Internal Medicine.

The study, conducted by doctors from the Chicago Centre for Clinical Research, found that women receiving a combination of oestrogen and the cholesterol drug pravastatin achieved the greatest improvement in cholesterol levels.

"These findings support the position ... that oestrogen, with a progestin where indicated, should be given consideration as a therapeutic option for the management of hypercholesterolemia in postmenepausal women," the researchers wrote in a report released on Sunday.
The study found that hormone treatment increased levels of high-density lipoprotein, the so-called "good" cholesterol, and lowered the leven of low-density lipoproteins, or "bad" cholesterol.
In women who were treated with a combination of oestrogen and pravastatin, the bad cholesterol level was reduced by nearly 29 percent while the good cholesterol rose by 21 percent, the study found.
In women treated with oestrogen alone, the bad cholesterol level dropped by 13 percent while the good cholesterol rose by 23 percent.
Women given only pravastatin showed a 25 percent drop in bad cholesterol and a only a 4 percent increase in good cholesterol.

"Since 30-35 percent of postmenopausal women women in the United States are potential candidates for pharmacological therapy ... the clinical and public health implications are substantial," the researchers wrote.
